title: feat(ui): show the Gateway connection state in the sidebar footer

commit.messageHeadline: feat(ui): show connection state at bottom left in every layout
test(ui): move footer status cases to the dot and chip contract
test(ui): follow connection status into the bottom-left chip
test(ui): scope readiness reconnect wait to the status chip
fix(ui): announce each connection transition once
fix(ui): keep connection announcements in the shell
fix(ui): position the connection chip without anchor support
fix(ui): keep the connection chip above sticky save bars
Merge branch 'main' into steipete/offline-status
fix(ui): prevent pet motion from overflowing composers
test(ui): await guest model switch settlement
fix(ui): anchor status chip to the bottom-left chat pane
refactor(ui): drop unreachable anchor fallback for the status chip
Merge origin/main into steipete/offline-status
Merge origin/main into steipete/offline-status
feat(ui): move connection state into the sidebar footer
fix(ui): keep the collapsed connection flag reachable
fix(ui): keep connection flags clear of writing surfaces
fix(ui): retain connection footer when settings cannot load
Merge origin/main into steipete/offline-status
fix(ui): restore header and footer presentation after merge
fix(ui): defer settings sidebar state preparation
Merge origin/main into steipete/offline-status
fix(ui): derive lazy settings sidebar props from its renderer
Merge origin/main into steipete/offline-status

Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR replaces layout-dependent connection labels with an avatar dot and a fixed bottom-left status chip while preserving Settings save feedback. **Example:** The desktop Gateway disconnects with two chat messages queued. - **Before:** Connection text is clipped inside the navigation rail. - **After:** A visible chip reads “Reconnecting… · 2 queued” and offers Retry now. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Useful and focused direction, with two concrete repairable defects and the required visual evidence still absent; no persistent format changes require migration. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Users cannot readily see connection loss in the desktop rail, and alternative status rows move the page while Settings loses save feedback. **Reason:** The source verifies the visibility problem, and this maintainer-authored PR supplies the direction for relocating its presentation. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 2 items remain** Keep this PR open: it addresses a current visibility defect with approved maintainer direction, but introduces duplicate accessibility announcements and a deterministic browser-test failure. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `18464294955a565c2f318835953e3b3bbd05eaf5` ## Before merge - [ ] **Keep a single live region for connection transitions (P2)** - With the regular desktop sidebar mounted, the shell now renders this unconditional polite live region alongside the existing sidebar region at app-sidebar-render.tsx:282. Reconnecting, suspension, and other unhealthy transitions therefore publish the same status twice to assistive technology. This independently confirms the existing review comment. Consolidate announcements at one owner while preserving recovery announcements when the sidebar is hidden or replaced by Settings. - [ ] **Scope the readiness test to one connection control (P2)** - The offline readiness case uses getByRole('button', { name: /Reconnecting…/ }). Showing the shell Retry button alongside the identity button makes that locator match two elements. The exact-head checks-ui-e2e (8/9) annotation reports this strict-mode failure at this line. Scope the locator to the intended identity control or shell chip so the readiness scenario can continue without weakening its assertions. ## Findings - [P2] Keep a single live region for connection transitions — `ui/src/components/solid/gateway-status.tsx:41` - [P2] Scope the readiness test to one connection control — `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e-readiness.e2e.test.ts:126` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply inspected before/after browser captures of the chip across desktop, mobile composer, and Settings recovery states; a base-fail/head-pass run for the added regression coverage is not shown.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main CSS clips the connection label inside the persistent rail, and the shell suppresses its alternative surface when that sidebar is available; no target code was executed during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? A fixed shell-owned chip directly addresses visibility and layout movement without changing connection state ownership, but its accessibility cutover must include the retained sidebar announcement.
